title: Per-Caller Concurrency, Graceband Entitlements, and Billing PRD
creator: Maya Chen
description: Define product requirements, acceptance criteria, and billing rules for per-caller concurrency limits plus a short-term graceband (soft overage window) for plan entitlements. This PRD clarifies how concurrency is enforced at the caller/API-key level, how a configurable graceband functions, and how overages are reported and invoiced.
goals: Provide deterministic per-caller concurrency enforcement to protect tenant SLAs and serving pools
Introduce a configurable graceband window that allows short bursts above entitlement without immediate billing or rate-limited rejections
Ensure billing and usage records accurately reflect bursts and soft overage behavior for transparent invoices
Minimize customer surprises and reduce support load by surfacing clear telemetry and notifications
requirements: Per-caller concurrency limit: each API key/caller must have an integer concurrency cap configurable per plan
Enforcement mode: hard limit (reject with HTTP 429) after graceband + margin exhausted, soft mode during graceband
Graceband configuration: duration in seconds (default 30s), maximum burst allowance expressed as percentage of entitlement or additional concurrent slots
Telemetry emitted: concurrency_current, concurrency_peak_window, graceband_start, graceband_end, overage_seconds
Billing recording: aggregate graceband usage separately from hard overage; billable units must be normalized to token-equivalent cost model
Admin controls: per-tenant override, per-route exemptions, and opt-in/opt-out for graceband automatic billing
Notifications: automated email/console alerts at 80% entitlement, when graceband is entered, and when hard limit rejections occur
Backoff guidance: include Retry-After headers and recommended exponential backoff in responses when rejecting requests
Audit logs: record decisions for enforcement with timestamps and decision rationale for compliance
acceptance_criteria: Given an API key with concurrency entitlement N and graceband configured for 30s/25% burst, short bursts up to N*(1+0.25) sustained for <=30s do not trigger immediate 429 responses
When bursts exceed graceband duration, requests beyond N are rejected with HTTP 429 and a Retry-After indicating when caller can retry
Billing export shows a separate line item for graceband usage (seconds * average concurrency over window) vs hard overage charges
Telemetry dashboard shows per-tenant concurrency_peak_window over 1m/5m/1h and clearly marks graceband windows
Admin console allows toggling graceband per-tenant and setting percent-based or absolute-slot burst allowances
Unit and e2e tests simulate concurrency patterns and validate enforcement and billing events with test harness (coverage >= 90% for enforcement logic)
Latency and P99 for unaffected tenants remain within SLOs during non-excessive graceband usage (no more than 3% SLO degradation in load tests)
billing_impact: Introduce new invoice line items: 'Graceband burst seconds' and 'Hard overage concurrency units'. Graceband is billed at a discounted rate relative to hard overage by default. Billing system must ingest graceband summary objects from telemetry pipeline daily and include them in invoice reconciliation. Usage attribution must be deterministically idempotent to support corrections.
scope: Implement per-caller concurrency enforcement in the request router/runtime
Graceband window engine in the quota service to track transient burst state
Telemetry signals and dashboard visualizations for graceband and concurrency peaks
Billing pipeline changes to accept graceband records and produce invoice line items
Admin UI controls for plan-level and tenant-level graceband configuration
out_of_scope: Per-user per-route adaptive concurrency algorithms (future work)
Automatic plan upgrades when persistent overage occurs (handled by separate churn playbook)
Complex pro-rata refund automation for historical graceband disputes (handled by billing ops manual process)
On-prem/private deployment differences for enforcement (assume cloud control-plane managed first)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal-only): deploy enforcement behind a feature flag for sandbox tenants and internal orgs; collect telemetry and smoke test
Phase 2 (beta): offer opt-in to select customers with console toggle and credits applied for early testing
Phase 3 (gradual): enable by default for new tenants and offer a 30-day migration window for existing tenants with billing preview
Phase 4 (GA): fully enable and include graceband line items on standard invoices
notes: Trade-offs documented: graceband reduces noisy 429s for short bursts but introduces billing complexity and potential tail latency risks. Default discount on graceband is intended to be conservative to avoid revenue leakage. Legal and finance must approve invoice labeling before GA.
